I NTRODUCTION W ith a view to addressing and, wherever possible, avoiding interpersonal conflicts simple and reliable informal mechanism s consisting in Facilitation and Mediation are required through the provision of external Mediators . P revention I n order to create a positive working environment, the Agency’s focus in the first instance is on conflict prevention. If and when tensions arise, they need to be addressed as early as possible in order to avoid long- lasting conflicts and aggravation. In t he case of interpersonal difficulties, it is essential that conflicts are addressed as early as possible and at the lowest level of intervention. Ideally, raising the matter directly with the person concerned is the best way to resolve issues . I nformal and formal mechanisms As t here is no one way of pre venting or resolving conflict, d ifferent informal and formal mechanisms exist to address conflicts when they arise and need to be applied according to the specific circumstances of each case. I t is theref ore strongly advised to seek the resolution of the problem through informal mechanisms first with the possible involvement of the Conflict Navigato

e specific circumstances of each case. I t is theref ore strongly advised to seek the resolution of the problem through informal mechanisms first with the possible involvement of the Conflict Navigators and/or the Mediators. T he advantage of the informal procedure over the formal procedure lies in the poss ibly of finding an amicable settlement of the situation in shorter timeframes thereby avoiding any further deterioration in the working environment. H aving recourse to the Mediators does not preclude application of the formal procedures provided for in the Staff Regulations, Rules and Instructions. 2. P OLICY I t is the Agency’s policy to introduce informal mechanism s (Facilitation and Mediation) allowing the resolution of interpersonal disputes within the Agency. 3. S COPE T he present Instruction applies to all cases of interpersonal dispute in the workplace between : − st aff members ; and − staff members and on - site contractors ’ personnel, or research fellows or trainees i rrespective of if the reference to articles in the Staff Regulations applies only to ESA staff. DEFINITIONS Within the scope of this Instruction, the following definit ions apply: Applicant to Facilitation or Mediation is a person within the scope of the instruction defined in section 3 above that is applying to the Coordinating Mediator to resolve an interpersonal conflict b etween himself and another P arty. Parties to Facilitation or Mediation are persons within the scope of the instruction defined in section 3 above that have recourse to one of these informal mechanisms to resolve an interpersonal conflict between them. Facilitation is the use of a neutral third party to help P arties identify potential issues ( such as tensions between viewpoints, interpersonal or other relationship issues) and facilitate constructive communication, collaborative problem solving and decision - making. Mediation is the use of a neutral third party to help P arties reach a voluntary resolution of a dispute which P arties have been unwilling or unable to resolve on their own. Mediation is a structured process that starts with the signing of a mediation agreement, after which the me diator will engage the P arties in confidential discussions based on interests rather than positions and help them negotiate an amicable settlement. A successful mediation results in a written, signed agreement set

gage the P arties in confidential discussions based on interests rather than positions and help them negotiate an amicable settlement. A successful mediation results in a written, signed agreement settling all matters in dispute. Mediators re fer s to both the Coordinating and Local Mediators , whose Terms of Reference and Status are defined in Annex 1 . Conflict Navigators are staff members with roles and responsibilities with regard to conflict prevention and resolution appointed by the Department in charge of personnel matters following consultation with the Staff A ssociation. 5. PRINCIPLES 5. 1 Voluntary participation Participation to Facilitation and Mediation is done on a voluntary basis. 5.2 Mediator’s right to decline a case Mediators may decline to examine any case submitted to them, stating their reasons for doing so . 5. 3 On - going d isciplinary p roceedings Where the Administration has initiate d disciplinary proceedings in accordance with Staff Regulation 26, the Mediators shall not be authorised to examine a case submitted to them if the case concerns the alleged offence subject to disciplinary proceedings. 5. 4 Impartiality The Coordinating Mediator and the Local Mediators shall perform their duties in a fu lly independent manner. The Mediators are neutral and impartial, which implies they do not take position or judge who is wrong or right. While in office, t

Mediators shall perform their duties in a fu lly independent manner. The Mediators are neutral and impartial, which implies they do not take position or judge who is wrong or right. While in office, they shall not hold any post or carry out any activity that might be considered to affect their impartiality. Such obligation shall continue indefinitely after the termination of their appointment. 5. 6 Security Marking of Communications C ommunications between the Mediators and between a Mediator and an A pplicant or any other person involved in a case treated by the Mediators are considered ESA Unclassified – Personnel in Confidence and shall therefore only be disclosed in accordance with section 3.4.6 of the ESA Security Directives and if duly authorised by the Media tors. 5. 7 Unauthorised disclosure U nauthorised disclosure by a staff member may constitute an offence liable to disciplinary action. U nauthorised disclosure by on - site contractor personnel may result in them being barred from ESA sites and in the termination of the contract with the Contractor responsible for such personnel. 6 . R OLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 6.1 Coordinating Mediator T he Coordinating Mediator is in charge of the coordination of a network of Local Mediators appointed by the Director General and established in the countries where ESA has its Establishments. T he Coordinating Mediator shall examine the applications and endeavour to bring about an amicable settlement between the P arties within reasonable time limits using the two alternative dispute resolution techniques: Facilitation or Mediation. S hould the Coordinating Mediator find that it is not possible to propose Facilitation or Mediation, he/she shall inform the Parties accordingly. 6.2 Local Mediators T he Local Mediat or s shall examine the applications and endeavour to bring about an amicable settlement between the P arties within reasonable time limits using the two alternative dispute resolution techn iques : Facilitation or M ediation . S hould the Local Mediator find that it is not possible to propose F acilitation or Mediation, he/she shall inform the P arties accordingly. 6.3 Conflicts Navigators C onflict Navigators shall provide the Coordinating Mediator and the Local Mediators with practical arrangement s and administrative support they require in order to carry out their duties. An A pplicant may request for F acilitation or M ediation in French or English, by email or telephone call to the Coordinating Mediator. The primary role of the Coordinating Mediator is to proceed with a screening of the application, i n particular whether proposing F acilitation o r M e diation to the Applicant, and appointment of a Mediator . 2. A rticle 3 – Working methods 1. U pon first contact, the Mediator shall begin any attempt of interpersonal dispute resolution b y lis tening to the Applicant in an open mind and understanding manner . As a first step, wher e a ppropriate, the Mediator shall try, by identifying and reframing issues and by developing a range of options, to help the A pplicant develop new ways to solve the problems on his/her own accord . Should such an approach prove unsuccessful , the Mediator shall attempt to reach a n am icable settlement through F acilitation or Mediation as described below. 2. T he Mediator sha ll proceed with face - to - face discussion s , when possible, or by web conferencing, with each of the P arties in dispute. At this stage, the Medi ator , i n cases of low severity of the conflict, shall propose F acilitation to the P arties. If, however the conflict has started to crysta l lize, the Mediator shall try to reach a proposal for Mediati on. 3. In such an agreement, the Mediator shall also establish a calendar taking into account the legal and administrative constraints, as well as the urgency of finding a soluti on. I n the discharge of their duties, the Mediators are bound to an obligation of confidentiality wit h r espect to any information disclosed to them in the course of their duties, including the ini tiation of a M ediation procedure, except where the Parties consent in writing to the disclosure and even then at the sole discretion of the Mediators. The only exception to this obligation to confidentiality is where there appears to be an imminent ser ious risk to life, health or integrity of persons, or to property, and where there is no other reasonable option than disclosure to the extent necessary to prevent the harm. Whether this risk exists is a determination to be made by the Mediators. 8. Wh en ca rrying out their mandate, the Mediators shall take account of the ESA Convention, the Staff Regulations, Rules and Instructions, the Pension Scheme Rules and Instructions, the internal provisions adopted in application of these texts, the ESA Charter of Va lues and guiding principles, all other rules governing ESA, as well as in a supplemental

T he Mediators perform their duties at ESA Establishments or at their professional office . A rticle 4 – End of the procedure 1. T he procedure shall end either: a. with the adoption of an amicable settlement by the P arties, or, b. if Mediators decline a case as provided for under section 5.2 - Principles of the present Instruction, c. if Mediators do not reach an amicable settlement . 2. The work carried out by the Mediators shall remain ESA Unclassified - Personnel in Confidence upon completion of the procedure unless the Parties request disclosure and even then at the sole discretion of the Mediators. All documents concerning the P arties involved in the M ediati on sh all be destroyed at the Mediators' discretion and at the latest at the end of their term of office or if Mediators decline a case pursuant to section 5. 2 – Principles of the present Instruction , w hichever is the latest. ticle 5 – Relations with formal procedures 1. S ubmitting an application for F acilitation or M ediation per se neither interrupts nor suspends the time limits applicable to the Advisory Board and Appeals Board in the Staff Regulations, ESA/ADMIN/IPOL - WORK (2019)1 Annex 2 P a g e 3 Rules and Instructions. The Mediators shall draw the A pplicant’s attention to these time limits when necessary, in particular by mentioning the possibility to appeal and providing the necessary information, subject to the procedure set out in the Staff Regulations, Rules and Instructions. 2. T he A pplicant may however, in the course of the F acilitation or M ediation proce ss, decide to safeguard his/her right to appeal by submitting a claim to the Director General within the time limits and subject to the procedure set out in the Staff Regulations, Rules and Instructions. The appeal shall contain a request for a suspension of the claim procedure pending the finalization of the F acilitation or M ediation process . 3. A n application for Facilitation or Mediation may not be filed with the Mediators if the A pplican t ha s already sought the opinion of the Advisory Board, lodged an appeal with the Appeals Board relating to the same matter or if an investigation process in relation with a complaint for harassment has been launched. E very year the Coordinating Mediator shall present a consolidated activity report of his/her office and of the Local Mediators office to the Director General, while respecting confidentiality and anonymity, stating the number and nature of the cases referr ed to them, whether they resorted to Facilitation or M ediation and were solved and, where applicable, what obstacles, in their opinion, prevented solutions from being found. The report may also mention cases that raise general questions relating to human r esources or administrative management , o r ethical matters. 2. I n their annual report, the Coordinating Mediator may make recommendations and suggest amendments to the regulatory framework and administrative practices. 3. T he Director General shall have the a nnual report published for official use only, unless he decides otherwise, and shall have the necessary follow -up action taken. 4. T he Coordinating Mediator may also present to Council and the Director General any other reports they deem necessary within the scope of activities of the Mediators.

ESA PENALTY POLICY The Industrial Policy Committee approved an ESA Penalty Policy (“Policy”) at its meeting in September 2014. In the Policy, four categories of contracts are defined and the penalty approach is described for each category (see table below). The Policy is applicable to fully funded contracts (i.e. nominally excluding programmes whose implementing rules explicitly foresee co ‐ funding by Industry) that result in delivery of items, goods, products and/or documentation and where the ESA GCC mandatorily applies. The table below summarises the Policy, the purpose of which is mainly to provide economic operators with an increased transparency and predictability with respect to the penalty clause in ESA contracts. ESA UNCLASSIFIED – Releasable to the Public ESA /REG/001,REV.6 Paris, 04 November 2024 (Original: English) REGULATIONS OF THE EUROPEAN SPACE AGENCY ESA Contracting Regulations and related Implementing Instructions The purpose of the attached Contracting Regulations and their Annexes (Implementing Instructions) is to regulate the Tender Process (as defined therein) for the execution of the European Space Agency (ESA) activities and programmes, in accordance with the ESA industrial policy objectives set out in A rticle VII of its Convention and Annex V thereto. In accordance with Article 48 thereto, the Contracting Regulations may be amended by the ESA Council on the recommendation of the Industrial Policy Committee and of the Administrative and Finance Committee. The Contracting Regulations have been approved by the ESA Council at its meeting on 23 - 24 October 2024 (ESA/C(2024)115) . They enter into force on 1 January 2025, when they replace ESA/REG/001, REV . 5 (ESA Procurement Regulation s and related Implementing Instructions ). Open competitive tender shall be the normal procedure for the placing of Contracts. 2. Restricted competitive tender may be applied: a) for the Procurement of goods or services the special nature of which limits the capacity to procure them from certain Economic Operators only; b) for those General Procurements where the time and cost required to examine and evaluate a large number of tenders would be disproportionate to the value of the goods or services to be procured; c) for the Procurement of goods or services by the Agency in the framework of international agreements entered into by the Agency with its Member States or public bodies (including international organisations), if expressly provided for in these agreements; d) where the goods or services are procured by the Agency by means of a Framework Agreement as defined under Article 8, paragraph 1 of these Regulations; e) for goods or services whose supply and performance must be accompanied, respectively, by special

ncy by means of a Framework Agreement as defined under Article 8, paragraph 1 of these Regulations; e) for goods or services whose supply and performance must be accompanied, respectively, by special security measures in accordance with the Agency’s Security Regulations (ESA/REG/004) in their latest applicable version, or when the protection of the essentia l security interest of the Agency requires; f) pursuant to a decision, guideline or policy of the Industrial Policy Committee in application of Article 3, paragraph 1 d) of these Regulations. 3. Wherever possible for restricted competitive tender, at least 3 (three) Economic Operators shall be invited to tender. 4. The reason for applying restricted competitive tender and the reason for the choice of the Economic Operators invited to submit a tender shall be recorded in the Contract File. ARTICLE 5 – NON - COMPETITIVE TENDERING 1. Competitive tendering may be waived in one or more of the following cases: a) if only one source for the goods or services exists; b) in case of extreme urgency resulting from compelling operational needs; c) where, for scientific, technical or economic reasons, Contracts for additional or supplementary goods or services cannot be separated from those of a previous Contract; ESA UNCLASSIFIED – Releasable to the Public ESA/REG/001,REV.6 Page 7 / 55 d) if the goods or services required are subject to

Where, following a competitive tender, only one tender is admitted, the Invitation to Tender shall be re - issued, unless it is considered that such re - issuing would be unlikely to obtain better results or would not be feasible due to extreme urgency resulti ng from compelling operational needs. Should such a situation arise, competitive tendering may be waived. 3. Where the goods or services are procured by the Agency in the framework of international agreements entered into by the Agency with its Member States or public bodies (including international organisations), competitive tendering may be waived if expressly provided for in those agreements. 4. Article 25 of these Regulations shall not apply when competitive tendering is waived. ARTICLE 6 – TWO - STAGE TENDERING 1. In order to obtain the most satisfactory solution to its Procurem

ARTICLE 1: RATIONALE OF ATTRIBUTION OF NATIONALITY TO COMPANIES FOR GEOGRAPHICAL RETURN PURPOSES AND CONDUCT OF RELEVANT AUDITS One of the main orientations governing the ESA industrial policy is the geo - return principle which enables the Executive to conduct and implement an effective European Space programme. This policy is based on all ESA Member States participating – having due regard to their financial contribution - in an equitable manner to the successful creation of a strong and competitive European industrial base for space activities. In order to provide for an equal and transparent treatment of all companies and furthermore to ensure an effective and accurate reporting on the industrial return statistics to the Member States, the objective of ESA audits in relation to the nationality o f companies, is to be assured or alternatively obtain evidence that an enterprise can effectively be considered to belong to specific ESA Member States, allowing as such the (parts of the - ) contracts awarded to this company to be coun

ernatively obtain evidence that an enterprise can effectively be considered to belong to specific ESA Member States, allowing as such the (parts of the - ) contracts awarded to this company to be counted as realised indu strial return for those specific Member States . The Article II.3 of Annex V to the ESA Convention lays down the following 4 main criteria in order to determine the nationality of a company: Criteria 1: Location of the enterprise registered office Criteria 2: Location of decision - making centres Criteria 3: Location of research centres Criteria 4: Territory on which the work is carried out Additional evaluation elements can be set in specific cases (e.g. for the industrial contracts of the Guiana Space Centre), and duly reported in procurement and/or audit documentation. With respect to the above criteria it is recalled that the Convention describes that in doubtful ESA UNCLASSIFIED – Releasable to the Public ESA/REG/001,REV.6 Annex II Page 4 / 7 cases the ESA Council shall decide whether an enterprise shall be considered to belong to one of the Member States, or not. For this specific task the Council has empowered the IPC, in accordance with section 7(a) of the IPC Terms of Reference (ESA/C/CLX/Res.1 (final)) This implementing instruction formalises the Agency’s audit methodology, procedure and approval process to establish the nationality of companies.
